title: Introduction to Programming
syllabus: Basics of programming using C; Basic UNIX commands, Primitives and Datatypes, Arithmetic operations, Input and output functions; Conditional statement; Loops, Introduction to Functions, Macros, Recursion, Arrays, Strings, Dynamic Memory Allocation, Pointers, Complex Data Types, File Handling, Introduction to Linked List, sorting, Searching, Bitwise Operator.

title: Mathematics-I
syllabus: Real number system: Sequences: Convergence of a sequence, Sandwich theorem, Cauchy sequences, subsequence, monotone sequences, monotone convergence theorem; Series: Convergence of infinite series, comparison test, Cauchy condensation test, ratio test, root test, Leibnitz test; Functions of one variable: Limits and continuity of functions, intermediate value property, differentiability, local maxima and minima, Rolles theorem, mean value theorem; Integration: Definite integrals, fundamental theorems of calculus, improper integrals; Functions of two variables: Limit, continuity, partial derivatives, directional derivatives, gradient, differentiability, chain rule, tangent planes, maxima and minima, Lagrange multiplier; Multiple integrals: Double and triple integrals, Green theorem, vector fields.

title: Mathematics-II
syllabus: Systems of linear equations: Elementary operations, row-reduced echelon matrices, Gauss elimination, LU factorization, linear independence, rank, solutions of linear systems; Vector spaces: Subspaces, spanning space, bases and dimensions; Linear transformations: Matrix representations, range space, rank, null space, nullity theorem, invertibility; Eigenvalues and eigenvectors: Hermitian, unitary matrices, eigen bases; Diagonalization: Cayley-Hamilton theorem, quadratic form; Inner product spaces: Orthonormal bases, Gram-Schmidt process; Differential Equations: First Order ODE, Lipschitz condition, Picard theorem; Linear differential equations: Wronskian, higher order constant coefficients, Cauchy-Euler equations, Laplace Transform.

title: Basic Electronics Engineering
syllabus: Semiconductor Diode, V-I characteristics, Half-Wave and Full-Wave Rectifier Circuits. Transistors: Bipolar Junction Transistor, MOSFET: Biasing, Small Signal model, Amplifiers. Operational Amplifiers: Ideal Op-Amp, applications (rectifiers/clipping, switching). ADC implementation; Logic Gates and Combinational Circuits: Number Systems and Binary Codes, Boolean Algebra, DeMorgans Theorems, SOP and POS Forms, K-Map Method, Combinational Logic Circuits, Half and Full adder-subtractor, Comparators, Multiplexers, Decoders/encoders; Synchronous and Ripple Counters; Communications overview.

title: Discrete Mathematics
syllabus: Sets, relations, functions, Equivalence and Partial order relations; Formal logic: Propositional logic and truth tables, normal forms, Predicates and Quantification; Notion of proof: proof techniques, Mathematical Induction; Combinatorics: Basic counting techniques, Pigeonhole principle, countable and uncountable sets, recurrence relations, Inclusion-exclusion principle; Graph theory: Graph terminology, representation, Isomorphism, trees, Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs, Graph coloring, Planar graphs; Number theory: Divisibility, GCD, Euclidean algorithm, Fundamental theorem of arithmetic, Modular arithmetic; Group theory: Groups, subgroups, cyclic groups, permutation groups.

title: Data Structures
syllabus: Stacks, Queues, Lists; Sorting and Searching; Trees, Tree Traversals; Heaps, Binary Search; Binary Search Trees, Balanced BSTs; Graphs: Representations, Depth First Search, Breadth First Search.

title: Software Tools & Technologies Lab
syllabus: Basics of Linux: Linux commands – text editors; Scripting languages; Web programming; Plotting tools; Document processing tools; Version control systems (Git); Debuggers, such as gdb; Containerization with Docker.

title: Probability and Statistics
syllabus: Introduction to set algebra, sigma algebra, Borel sigma algebra, sequence of sets and limits; Axiomatic definition of probability, probability space, conditional probability, Bayes rule, independence; Random variables, distribution functions, PMF and PDF, expectation, moments, MGF, Markov and Chebyshev inequality; Joint distributions, marginal and conditional distributions, covariance and correlation, Central Limit Theorem, parameter estimation, hypothesis testing.

title: Computer Organization and Architecture
syllabus: Overview of basic digital building blocks, truth tables, basic structure of digital computer, number representation; Machine Instructions and Program: Assembly language programming; Arithmetic Unit: Building blocks for ALU, adder, subtractor, shifter, multiplication/division circuits, microprogramming, hardwired control; Memory organization: ROM, RAM, cache memories, cache coherence, virtual memory, secondary storage; Input/Output: I/O subblock, interrupts, polling, DMA; Pipelining: Instruction pipelines, hazards.

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
syllabus: Algorithm analysis: worst and average case, recurrences and asymptotes; Sorting and selection algorithms; Randomized techniques, Divide and Conquer; Dynamic programming and greedy algorithms; Graph algorithms: BFS, DFS and applications, MSTs, shortest paths; NP-Complete problems and Approximation Algorithms.

title: Theory of Computation
syllabus: Alphabets, languages, finite state machines (DFA, NFA); Context Free Grammars and Context-Free Languages, Parse trees, PushDown Automata, CYK algorithm; Turing machines and variants; Undecidability theory, Halting problem, Space and Time complexity, NP-Completeness.

title: Operating Systems
syllabus: Introduction to OS, Virtualization, Concurrency, Persistence; CPU Virtualization: Process, Process API, PCB, CPU Scheduling, Multilevel feedback queue; Memory Virtualization: Address space, Memory API, address translation, segmentation, paging, TLBs, replacement policies, swapping; Concurrency: threads, Thread API, locks, condition variables, semaphores, concurrency bugs; Persistence: I/O devices, Hard disks, RAID, file systems; OS Security: Authentication, access control; Tools: xv6.

title: Compiler Design
syllabus: Compiler structure: analysis-synthesis model of compilation, phases of compiler, tool-based approach; Lexical analysis (lex/flex); Syntax analysis (LL, LR, LALR parsers, yacc/bison); Syntax-directed translation; Type checking and semantic analysis; Run-time storage administration; Intermediate code generation; Machine-independent optimizations; Target code generation.

title: Database Management Systems
syllabus: Database System Concepts: Data models, schemas, instances, architecture; Relational Algebra: SELECT, PROJECT, set operations, JOIN, DIVISION; Entity-Relationship (ER) and Enhanced ER (EER) modeling, relational mapping; Normalization: Functional dependencies, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF; Database programming: SQL (DDL, DML, triggers, views), transaction management, ACID properties, indexing (B-trees, hashing).

title: Artificial Intelligence
syllabus: Introduction and Problem solving by search: State Space, Graph Search, A*, Heuristics, Adversarial Game Playing, Constraint Satisfaction; Automated Reasoning: Propositional and first-order logic, resolution refutation, knowledge representation; Planning: State-space and plan space planning; Reasoning under uncertainty: Probabilistic reasoning, Bayesian networks, Fuzzy logic; Reinforcement Learning: MDP, Q-Learning.

title: Computer Networks
syllabus: Layered architecture, packet switching, performance metrics; Application layer: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, P2P, CDN; Transport Layer: TCP, UDP, flow control, congestion control, QUIC; Socket Programming; Network Layer: IPv4, IPv6, addressing, CIDR, NAT, routing algorithms (OSPF, BGP), ICMP, ARP; Data Link Layer: framing, error detection/correction, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA, Ethernet, Wi-Fi; Network security basics, SDN.

title: AI-Augmented Software Development
syllabus: LLM-based software engineering: Role of LLMs in software lifecycle, testing, debugging, code generation, limitations; Prompting as interface design: Structured prompting, task specification; LLMs as software components: API integration, context handling, schema validation, retries; Agentic workflows: ReAct patterns, planner-executor, tool calling, memory management; Observability, test harnesses, safety, governance, and capstone system development.

title: Parallel Algorithms
syllabus: Models of parallel computation: PRAM models, interconnection networks, performance analysis; Basic parallel techniques: Matrix multiplication, parallel sorting, searching, selection, balanced trees, divide-and-conquer, pipelining, tree contraction, Euler tour; Parallel graph algorithms: Connected components, coloring, MST, shortest paths; Asynchronous models, NC-reductions, P-completeness.

title: Randomized Algorithms
syllabus: Introduction and basic tools: random sequences, pseudorandom generation, statistical tests (Chi-square); Game theoretic techniques: Yao principle; Moments and deviations: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities, Chernoff bounds, Martingales; Tail bounds applications; Randomized graph algorithms: Min-cut, random walks, Markov chains; Probabilistic method and derandomization.

title: Introduction to Computational Complexity
syllabus: Computational models, Turing Machines, Decidability, Reducibility; Time and Space Complexity, Time and Space Hierarchy Theorems; Non-deterministic computation, P vs NP, NP-completeness; Diagonalization limits; Oracle Turing Machines and the Relativization barrier; Space complexity classes (L, NL, PSPACE); Boolean circuits and Circuit Complexity; Randomized complexity classes (RP, BPP, ZPP).
